newsitem.title: USA: LDC debts seen outperforming U.S. bonds in 1997.
newsitem.headline: LDC debts seen outperforming U.S. bonds in 1997.

text.p: Ample global liquidity and greater acceptance of emerging markets as an asset class by portfolio managers has set the stage for another good year for emerging market bonds, experts at the annual conference of the Fixed Income Analysts Society said on Tuesday.
"The emerging market will outperform (other fixed income assets), but it will be leaner and more volatile" in 1997, said Jack Malvey, chief global fixed income strategist at Lehman Brothers.

The total return on the Lehman Brothers Emerging Americas index registered a 27.38 percent gain for the year-to-date, compared with a rise of 3.83 percent for U.S. government securities, 4.73 percent for investment grade corporates and 10.56 percent for high yield corporates.

Joseph Carson, chief economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said he expected Europe and Japan, which lag behind the U.S. in the economic cycle, to keep interest rates low, thus providing liquidity to the global market. "The liquidity will come from outside the U.S.," he said.

Patricia Cook, managing director of Fisher Francis Trees and Watts, said non-dollar markets expanded the scope of the investment universe for investors seeking enhanced yield and diversification. "It is a growing asset class," she said.
